subject: Cloudza SLA: multi-region failover & discount request
messages:
From: Diane Myers <diane@cloudza.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Cho <ben.cho@cloudza.com>
Date: 2026-09-17T08:23:00-07:00
Subject: SLA requirements and discount inquiry for Cloudza pilot

Hi Irene / Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Cloudza is planning a three-month pilot that could scale to multi-region production in Q1 if results look good. Before we lock dates, procurement needs clarity on a few SLA items and whether Redwood can provide a commercial concession for an initial commit.

High-level ask:
- Uptime tiers: We need a written guarantee for 99.9% and an optional 99.95% for a price uplift.
- Response windows: 4-hour P1 during business hours (M-F, 6am-8pm PT) and 24x7 on-call for P0 incidents.
- Regional failover: Can you include a cold failover for EU region that can be brought live within 2 hours?
- Pricing: For a 12-month commit (~$55k/mo committed usage forecast), is there a standard discount grid? We're targeting a 25% introductory discount in exchange for the commit and a case study.

Attached is our RFP and a short spreadsheet with expected token volumes. Can we get a written SLA proposal and cost options by early next week?

Best,
Diane
Diane Myers
Sr. Procurement Manager | Cloudza Inc.
attachments: Cloudza_RFP_SLA_20260915.pdf
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-18T10:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA requirements and discount inquiry for Cloudza pilot

Hi Diane — thanks for the clear summary and the RFP. Appreciate the volume detail.

Short answer up front: we can meet your response-window needs and we have a few commercial paths for the discount you're asking for. I've attached a concise proposal (SLA_Tiers_Proposal_v1.pdf) that outlines three options:

Option A — Standard: 99.9% uptime, P1 4hr business-hours response, P0 24x7 on-call. No failover included.
Option B — Resilient: 99.95% uptime, P1 2hr business-hours response, includes warm standby in a secondary region (failover time typically <2 hours with our runbook).
Option C — Enterprise: 99.99% with active-active across regions and a guaranteed 60s paged-alert triage.

Commercially: for a 12-month commit at your forecasted band we can offer:
- Option A: list price less 10% standard commit discount
- Option B: list price less 18% with a technical case study and standard payment terms
- Option C: custom pricing (requires dedicated capacity discussion)

We don't typically start at 25% off list for first-year pilots, but we can consider a promotional band between 15–20% with a short-term performance SLAs and early-renewal clause. Karthik and I flagged a possible one-year 20% introductory concession if Cloudza commits to the 12-month volume and agrees to a public case study/reference.

Next steps: would you be open to a 30-minute pricing + legal scoping call? Markus (VP Revenue) is on copy; if this looks like something we can agree to in principle, I'd like to bring him in to confirm exception authority.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0211

Hi Irene — thanks for the clear options. I shared internally and procurement pushed back on starting below 25% for the first year — they view the case study ask as reasonable but not sufficient to move from 25%. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The cold/warm standby behavior: cold is fine as long as your documented runbook shows a sub-2 hour RTO and an SLA-backed failover exercise in onboarding.
- Payment terms: can you consider Net 30? Procurement prefers Net 30 for pilots before scaling.
- Legal: we will need the standard security annex and our SOC-2 addendum accepted.

Attached is a short spreadsheet detailing our expected monthly spend per environment. If you can get to 20% plus Net 30 and confirm a documented failover runbook exercise by onboarding, we can push to approve. Otherwise procurement will ask us to continue negotiations.

Can we take your 20% offer and ask for a written exception memo (formal approval) from revenue leadership? If so, I'll align legal and procurement and get the MSA review started.

Thanks,
Diane

Subject: Re: SLA requirements and discount inquiry for Cloudza pilot

Diane — thanks for the patience and for laying out procurement's constraints. I'm Markus (VP Revenue) — looping in formally to confirm what we can approve.

Decision (summary):
- We can approve a one-year introductory concession of 20% off list for Option B (99.95% with warm standby) provided Cloudza:
  1) Signs a 12-month committed-spend agreement at the forecasted tier (CLD-9347 commitment)
  2) Agrees to Net 30 payment terms for the pilot period
  3) Provides Redwood a technical case study and reference within 90 days of production go-live

- Failover: we will include a documented failover runbook and a joint onboarding failover exercise (pre-production rehearsal). That exercise will be scheduled as part of the onboarding playbook and is covered in the pricing for Option B.

- Legal/security: our legal team will accept the SOC 2 addendum with standard carve outs — please share the addendum and Ben (cc) can coordinate.

Irene/Karthik: please prepare the exception memo for the 20% concession (include revenue impact, expected TCV, and reference commitment). Once legal gives a thumbs up, we can route a DocuSign link for signatures. Diane — I can send the DocuSign link once legal confirms language; we expect standard MSA plus the SLA exhibit.
